title: Shrimp and noodles with cream or white sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish combines broad noodles, sautéed shrimp, and a smooth cream or white sauce made from cream, milk and seasonings. Shrimp cook quickly, while the sauce gives the meal a velvety texture and notes of garlic, lemon and fresh herbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp are one of the most consumed seafood items worldwide, with demand growing over 5 % annually.
Durum‑wheat noodles retain their shape even after prolonged simmering in sauce.
Cream sauce is often thickened with a roux of flour and butter before adding 10‑20 % cream.
The recipe can be adapted for lighter diets by using low‑fat milk or plant‑based cream alternatives.
Asian variations often add ginger and soy sauce for a more pronounced flavor.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Shrimp provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of shrimp contain roughly 99 kcal, making them suitable for weight‑control meals.

items.title: Source of omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: EPA and DHA in shrimp contribute to heart and brain health.

items.title: Rich in vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for blood formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace elements support immune defense and antioxidant processes.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Prepared sauces can be salty; adjust added salt to taste.

items.title: Foodborne pathogens
items.content: Improperly stored shrimp may harbor bacteria that cause food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the noodles al dente, sauté the shrimp with garlic, then add cream, milk, lemon juice and seasonings. Toss the sauce with the noodles, garnish with fresh herbs, grated Parmesan or a lemon wedge, and serve hot.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw shrimp refrigerated at 0‑2 °C for up to 2 days or freeze them. Leftover cooked dish should be consumed within 24 hours, stored in an airtight container in the fridge.
